geometry_notes: W6 line is ~3.5 m too far south for s 3-15: lidar is ground (0 m) 1-2 m inside it while the roof (11.8 m) starts ~4 m inside. Move W6 north ~3.5 m (or the annex's south face is set back from the B1 junction).

The annex (inside W4/W5/W6 and the W3 line extended) is open at ground for 3.6 m (a public walk-through); the model should hollow it with columns rather than draw a solid block. Its east side is ESC's brick west wall continuing the W3/W7 line (17.75 m) with glazed doors.
W4: lidar roof reaches ~2 m beyond the W4 line: the window boxes cantilever past it.

Ground is not flat: the lawn court east of W11 s 0-15, W10 and W9 is ~4.3 m above the west/south grade (DTM 335.0 vs 330.7-331.3); lidar roof heights of 8-9.6 m there are relative to that raised ground. The roof is one flat level at 342.9 m everywhere.
W0 has a 3-storey link block to C2 at s 9-13.5 (lidar 11.3 m) that is not in the footprint.
A ~10.5 m mass joins W10 to EIT (lidar), unseen in photos.
notes: The main block is a plain late-1960s brown-brick slab whose identity is the rhythm of light-grey precast window strips (single at ends, paired elsewhere) between slim projecting brick pilasters; the white precast annex with its projecting window boxes over an open undercroft is the most recognisable piece, seen from the main N-S walkway. No web photos exist; everything is from Street View (2014-2019), the 2023 ortho and lidar.
